summary: Couch Investor reacts to the AI selloff triggered by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's 'we must pace the frontier' blog post warning of AI's existential risks. Monday's tape was mixed: Broadcom -4.7%, Nvidia -3.3%, Micron -5.2%, and neoclouds fell, while Google, Microsoft, Meta, cybersecurity and software names rallied, and Tuesday's pre-market showed semis bouncing. He dismisses the doomsday framing — if AI could destroy humanity, it can also be built to defend against bad AI — and sides with Jensen Huang, who called 10% extinction predictions fabricated and said sandboxing and verification solve safety issues. He notes Elon Musk agreed with Amodei but proposed competitor pre-release testing, China cooperation, and big-tobacco-level liability. The creator argues the labs' slowdown push is regulatory capture aimed at open-source/open-weights models (Meta) threatening their moats, since their subscription-only chatbot businesses are unsustainable, unlike the hugely profitable core businesses of Google and Meta. He calls Meta an $800 stock, still extremely undervalued, and expects Meta's Muse downloads to keep climbing. His macro framework: if AI capex growth slows, free cash flow at the hyperscalers surges while chip and memory makers get hurt; he walks through 2026-2028 capex estimates and covers AMD, Nebius, CoreWeave, Nvidia, Micron, Alphabet, and SpaceX. Call: META BUY.
